checks.name: step 1: create the case from the Phishing campaign template
step 2: add the source link and pull the 13 domains with Extract IOCs
step 3: delete unused placeholders, edit the operator and target cards
step 4: quick-add techniques, events and a note
step 5: arrange the board by dragging cards
step 6: connect the evidence with threads
step 6b: thread editor — record why two cards are linked
step 7: OSINT workbench on a domain
step 8: stamp and grade the indicators, add tasks
step 9: score the template hypotheses in ACH
step 10: key judgement, notes, snapshot, review state
step 13: case brief, STIX and case export

shots.title: Step 1 · Start the case
shots.caption: Click New case and choose the Phishing campaign template. It pre-loads three hypotheses, seven starter cards and four tasks, and sets TLP:AMBER.

shots.title: Step 1 · The empty case
shots.caption: The new case opens with the template's starter cards pinned. Rename the case in the title box, type your name in Analyst (it is stamped on every log entry), and set the TLP. Public reporting goes in as TLP:GREEN.
marks: Starter cards from the template: lure domain, sender, landing page, technique, operator, target, first event

shots.title: Step 2 · Pull the indicators out of the report
shots.caption: Paste the brief's indicator list into Extract IOCs and press Extract. Every defanged domain is recognised and typed. Leave them all ticked and press "Pin selected to board".

shots.title: Step 3 · Flesh out the actors and victims
shots.caption: Click any card to edit it in the Inspector. Give the operator and target cards real titles and bodies, stamp what the source confirms, and record where each fact came from under SOURCE. Select a placeholder you do not need and press Delete.
marks: Operator card (stamped Unverified: no named group)
Target card with sector, region, impact
Inspector: title, body, stamp, tags, source

shots.title: Step 5 · Arrange the evidence
shots.caption: Drag cards to arrange them: dated events down the left, actor / victim / analyst notes next, the thirteen domains as a grid, ATT&CK techniques on the right. Drag empty board to pan, use the mouse wheel to zoom, press F to fit.
marks: Event cards (red edge) carry the date

shots.title: Step 6 · Thread the evidence
shots.caption: Press C (Connect), pick a relation on the toolbar, then click one card and another. "controls" for operator → infrastructure, "linked to" for evidence, "suspected" where the source hedges. Click a thread label to open the thread editor and write down why the two are connected; the case brief prints it.

shots.title: Step 7 · Pivot on an indicator
shots.caption: Select a domain card and press O (or OSINT). The selector is pre-filled; press Run. Live lookups that allow browser access (Google DNS, crt.sh, RDAP, …) return inline; the others are one-click launchers (VirusTotal, urlscan, Shodan, Wayback). "Copy findings" puts the results on the clipboard; pinning writes them into the card.

shots.title: Step 8 · Grade the evidence
shots.caption: For each key indicator: stamp it Confirmed, name the source, set the collection date and the Admiralty grade (B2 = usually reliable source, probably true). First seen / last seen feed the staleness check in the Audit tab.

shots.title: Step 8 · Tasks and comments
shots.caption: Further down the same card: the follow-up tasks (block, hunt in SSO logs, registrar abuse report) and a dated comment. Open tasks are listed in the Audit tab until they are ticked off.
marks: Comments, stamped with analyst and time

shots.title: Step 9 · Test the hypotheses
shots.caption: ACH: the template seeded three hypotheses. Click each cell to mark an exhibit Consistent (C) or Inconsistent (I) with a hypothesis. Repeated targeting, vendor-specific domains and live vishing are consistent with an organised crew and inconsistent with an opportunistic actor.
marks: Click a cell to cycle consistent → inconsistent → neutral

shots.title: Step 10 · Write the judgement
shots.caption: Write the key judgement in the Notes tab with a confidence level and the dissenting view. Keep the working theory and open questions in the notes. Save a named snapshot in the Log tab so you can diff the board later, and move the review state to "In review".

shots.title: Step 11 · Timeline
shots.caption: Press T for the timeline view: the dated cards line up from the July registration wave to the 19 Oct brief; undated cards sit on the shelf. The rail at the bottom lists the same events.

shots.title: Step 11 · Kill chain
shots.caption: Press K for kill-chain lanes: Resource Development (acquire domains) → Initial Access (vishing) → Credential Access (MFA request generation) → Valid Accounts, with the evidence threaded to each technique shown beneath it.

shots.title: Step 12 · Ask for the takedown
shots.caption: Requests → Takedown request. All indicators are pre-ticked; name the recipient and open the letter. It lists the domains defanged, the case number, TLP and your name, ready to paste into an abuse report.

shots.title: Step 13 · Report and share
shots.caption: The finished board. Case brief prints everything (judgement, exhibits, threads with their evidence, timeline, tasks) for PDF; STIX exports the indicators, techniques and relationships for MISP / OpenCTI; Export case saves the JSON you can re-import later.
